productContexts.label: Thick 3D assemblies prepared for Raman; Methods scope S1–S4
notes: The method text names S1–S4 for Raman assembly; Figure 4e/f shows 3.9 and 7.7 nm optical assembly contexts, and Figure 5a labels S1/S2/S6/S7 spectra. No exact sample-to-method reconciliation is given.

operationContexts.label: Horizontally immerse 10×5 mm HOPG substrate in Co NC solution
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Use the source dimensions 10 × 5 mm and 200 μL solution volume; this is a separate thick-assembly/Raman procedure.

operationContexts.label: Evaporate solvent at 35 °C under nitrogen flow
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: 35 °C applies only to thick-assembly solvent evaporation. Flow rate and duration are unreported; never attach this temperature to Co growth or Raman acquisition.

source_notes: Complete eight-page main-only review; independent source and canonical audit passed. Browser and release verification are separate.
SI not located or verified; no SI-only claims.
No sample/batch links beyond explicit source labels. Exact-coordinate and training eligibility are false.

§2.5 says the 35 °C thick 3D Raman procedure uses solutions S1–S4; Figure 4e/f depicts 3.9/7.7 nm thick-assembly contexts and Figure 5a labels S1, S2, S6, S7 spectra. Do not assert all these are the same batches or pick one scope.
Figure 5a S7 trace is labeled 9.1 nm; Table 2 and Figure 2a give 9.3 nm. The abstract endpoint is approximately 9.3 nm; no reconciliation is provided.
N₂ flow rate and evaporation duration; exact layer count/thickness; the methods S1–S4 Raman preparation scope is not reconciled to Figure 4e/f and Figure 5a sample labels.
Raman acquisition time and sample temperature; exact specimen/replicate identities for reported spectra; no numerical per-trace values are digitized.

intuition.title: Author-proposed solvent and size interpretation
intuition.summary: The authors relate solvent–AOT interaction parameters to ligand interactions/passivation and report a size trend. This is their interpretation of the reported calculated quantities; the paper’s Eq. 2/3 are retained with dimensional/log-base caveats and are not refit here.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
